newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends off on profit-taking, earnings jitters.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends off on profit-taking, earnings jitters.

text.p: U.S. stocks lost ground on profit-taking and caution ahead of the corporate earnings rush, keeping the Dow industrials from closing above the key 6000 level and other indices from notching new records.

"By and large, investors are hesitating, waiting to see what third-quarter earnings have in store before committing further. We've already had a four percent move up on the broader market in the last three to four weeks," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment strategist at Gruntal & Co.
After climbing 30 points earlier, the Dow lost 13 to 5967.
The S&P 500 lost three to about 701 after setting its second consecutive record closing high on Monday. The NYSE Composite lost one to about 374.
The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite, which Monday scored its first all-time high finish in four months, shed 11 to about 1240 as an early high-tech rally faded.

Bellwether Intel hit a fresh 52-week high of 107 after Merrill Lynch reiterated its positive view for the chip industry but then ended down 3-1/8 to 101-5/8 after Salomon Brothers downgraded the stock on price. Microsoft lost 2-1/8 to 135-3/8 after trading as high as 137-3/4 earlier.

Chip and cellular phone maker Motorola lost 3/4 to 48-1/2 after reporting a sharp drop in third-quarter earnings. The company said it expected to take a fourth-quarter charge as part of its efforts to cut costs in its semiconductor and other groups. PaineWebber downgraded Motorola.

"Investors have grown more fearful of third-quarter earnings in light of Motorola's disappointing results. In a conference call, management provided more cautious guidance for the future that rocked the tech sector," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management, which has $6 billion of assets under management.

Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott, said the market was consolidating recent strong gains. "There's not any kind of structure for a major decline. I do think the risk/reward factors are diminishing and investors are taking a selective look at the market."

Meanwhile, Wall Street was awaiting Friday's release of September producer prices and retail sales data. The long bond slipped 6/32 to yield 6.80 percent after a 10-year Treasury note auction attracted a little less demand than expected.
Among individual stocks, McDermott International lost 2-1/2 to 19-1/2 after an earnings warning.
American Brands rose 3-3/8 to 47-7/8 after news it plans to spin off its British-based Gallaher tobacco business and change its own name to Fortune Brands.

Dole Food lost 2-1/8 to 37-5/8 after news its chief financial officer has left to join Republic Industries. The CFO's departure comes in the wake of last week's forecast that third-quarter results would be at the low end of analyst forecasts. Lehman Brothers downgraded the stock.
Expeditors International, a transportation and logistics company, surged 4-3/4 to 40 after forecasting it would top analysts third-quarter earnings estimates by about 25 percent.
Xcellent rallied five to 18-5/8 after a Robertson Stephens upgrade.

Super Foods soared four to 15-1/4 after news it agreed to merge with Nash Finch, the fourth largest public grocery wholesaler. Terms provide for Nash Finch, up 1/4 to 16-3/4, to start a cash tender for all 11.2 million outstanding Super Foods shares for $15.50 a share.
Losers outpaced gainers 1361 to 1014 on heavy NYSE volume of 434.7 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 10.72 to 1240.15.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.70 to 700.64.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
